newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli industrialist assails Netanyahu policy.
newsitem.headline: Israeli industrialist assails Netanyahu policy.

text.p: A leading Israeli industrialist, in an interview published on Friday, called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a failure at management who had ignored Israel's business community.

"By me the prime minister is a director-general, and I want to know what his management plan is. I fear there isn't one," Benny Gaon, CEO of Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's largest holding company, told the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth.
He said Netanyahu's management was a "failing management".

Gaon acknowledged having supported assassinated prime minister Yitzhak Rabin and prime minister Shimon Peres, who launched the peace moves with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat which the right-wing Netanyahu reluctantly inherited with his election 11 months ago. But Gaon said that shouldn't stop Netanyahu from calling for advice.

"I told Netanyahu I am ready to be your bridge to the business community. Consult us, come to us, speak with us. It was like sending a fax without an answering system...Bibi doesn't answer," said Gaon, whose company does business in telecommunications and electronics, agrochemicals and building and infrastructure materials.
Netanyahu was in the Netherlands and Italy on Friday and his spokesman could not be reached for comment.

Israeli-Palestinian peace talks have been stuck since Netanyahu started work on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 and an explosion at a Tel Aviv cafe killed three Israeli women and the Palestinian bomber three days later.

Last September Netanyahu triggered violence, including gun battles, when he opened a tunnel near an Islamic shrine in East Jerusalem. Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers died in the fighting.

"After Netanyahu was elected, I sent calming letters to investors in the United States. I told them, give him a chance. By way of accomplishments he pulled out of Hebron and cut the budget," Gaon said.

"The world business community isn't ready to accept uncertainty. In every meeting I have with business people in the world I have to explain what is happening with us," said Gaon, whose company had revenues of $3.525 billion last year and a net profit of $180.84 million.

Gaon said that acting on Rabin's promise of a peace process, he had made deals with Arafat totalling $150 million a year and sells the Palestinian leader cement and pipes. He said he was building in Amman and had opened offices in Indonesia, China, India, Tanzania and the Philippines.
